title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第六: 耶律解里 耶律拔里得 耶律朔古 耶律魯不古 趙延壽 高模翰 趙思溫 耶律漚里思 張礪
title.en: Volume 76 Biographies 6: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, Zhang Li
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第六: 耶律解里 耶律拔里得 耶律朔古 耶律魯不古 趙延壽 高模翰 趙思溫 耶律漚里思 張礪 Volume 76 Biographies 6: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, Zhang Li

sentences.zh: 耶律解裏耶律拔裏得耶律朔古耶律魯不古趙延壽高模翰趙思溫耶律漚裏思張礪

translations.literal: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, Zhang Li.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, and Zhang Li.

sentences.zh: 耶律解裏，字潑單，突呂不部人，世為小吏。

translations.literal: Yelu Jieli, style name Podan, was a man of the Tulübu tribe; his family for generations served as petty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Jieli, whose style name was Podan, came from the Tulübu tribe; for generations his family had served as minor clerks.

sentences.zh: 解裏早隸太宗麾下，擢為軍校。

translations.literal: Jieli early served under Taizong's banner and was promoted to army commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli entered Taizong's service early and was raised to the rank of army commandant.

sentences.zh: 天顯間，唐攻定州，既陷，解裏為唐兵所獲。

translations.literal: During the Tianxian era, Tang attacked Ding Prefecture; after it fell, Jieli was captured by Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxian period, when Tang forces took Ding Prefecture, Jieli was captured by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖立，始歸國。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu was enthroned, he at last returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin Gaozu came to the throne, he was finally able to return home.

sentences.zh: 太宗貰其罪，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Taizong pardoned his offense and appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong forgave his offense and made him Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會同九年伐晉，師次滹沱河，奪中渡橋，降其將杜重威。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huitong, campaigning against Jin, the army halted at the Hutuo River, seized Zhongdu Bridge, and induced its general Du Chongwei to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Huitong year nine, on the campaign against Jin, the army camped at the Hutuo River, took Zhongdu Bridge, and brought Du Chongwei to surrender.

sentences.zh: 上命解裏與降將張彥澤率騎兵三千疾趨河南，所至無敢當其鋒。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Jieli and the surrendered general Zhang Yanze to lead three thousand horsemen in a rapid advance into Henan; wherever they went none dared meet their edge.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Jieli and the surrendered general Zhang Yanze to lead three thousand cavalry in a swift drive into Henan; no one along their route dared stand against them.

sentences.zh: 既入汴，解裏等遷晉主重貴於開封府。

translations.literal: After entering Bian, Jieli and the others moved Jin ruler Chonggui to Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had entered Bian, Jieli and his party relocated the Jin emperor Chonggui to Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彥澤恣殺掠，亂宮掖，解裏不能禁，百姓騷然，莫不怨憤。

translations.literal: Yanze wantonly killed and plundered and threw the inner palace into disorder; Jieli could not restrain him, the common people were in uproar, and none failed to resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze slaughtered and looted at will and threw the inner palace into chaos; Jieli could not stop him, the populace seethed, and resentment was universal.

sentences.zh: 車駕至京，數彥澤罪，斬於市，汴人大悅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached the capital, he enumerated Yanze's crimes and executed him in the market; the people of Bian were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession reached the capital, the Emperor recited Yanze's crimes and had him beheaded in the marketplace, to the great joy of Bian's people.

sentences.zh: 解裏亦被詰責，尋釋之。

translations.literal: Jieli too was called to account, but was soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli was rebuked as well, though he was released shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 天祿間，加守太子太傅。

translations.literal: During the Tianlu era, he was further made acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianlu period he was additionally appointed acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，置本部令穩，解裏世其職，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli, the office of tribal chieftain was established; Jieli inherited the post by descent and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingli, when the tribal chieftainship was instituted, Jieli held the post by hereditary succession until his death.

sentences.zh: 耶律拔裏得，字孩鄰，太祖弟剌葛之子。

translations.literal: Yelu Balide, style name Hailin, was a son of Taizu's younger brother Cige.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Balide, styled Hailin, was the son of Taizu's younger brother Cige.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以親愛見任。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Balide was trusted for his close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession, Balide won trust through close family ties.

sentences.zh: 會同七年，討石重貴，拔裏得進圍德州，下之，擒刺史師居璠等二十七人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huitong, campaigning against Shi Chonggui, Balide advanced to besiege De Prefecture, took it, and captured the prefect Shi Jufan and twenty-seven others.
translations.idiomatic: In Huitong year seven, on the expedition against Shi Chonggui, Balide pressed the siege of De Prefecture, captured it, and took the prefect Shi Jufan and twenty-seven others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 九年，再舉兵，次滹沱河，降杜重威，戰功居多。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again raised troops, halted at the Hutuo River, and induced Du Chongwei to surrender; his battle merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he marched again, camped at the Hutuo River, and brought Du Chongwei to surrender, earning the greatest share of merit in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 太宗入汴，以功授安國軍節度使，總領河北道事。

translations.literal: When Taizong entered Bian, for his merit he was made military commissioner of Anguo Army and given overall charge of affairs on the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong entered Bian, Balide was appointed military commissioner of the Anguo Army and put in overall charge of the Hebei circuit for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 師還，州郡往往叛，以應劉知遠，拔裏得不能守而歸。

translations.literal: When the army returned, prefectures and districts often rebelled to join Liu Zhiyuan; Balide could not hold them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, many prefectures and districts rose for Liu Zhiyuan; Balide could not keep them and fell back.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷中京留守，卒。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was transferred to garrison commander of the Central Capital and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's accession he was made garrison commander of the Central Capital, where he died.

sentences.zh: 耶律魯不古，字信寧，太祖從侄也。

translations.literal: Yelu Lubugu, style name Xining, was a son of Taizu's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Lubugu, whose style name was Xining, was a younger cousin of Taizu on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖制契丹國字，魯不古以贊成功，授林牙、監修國史。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Taizu devised the Khitan national script, Lubugu aided the achievement and was appointed Yelu, supervisor of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Taizu created the Khitan script, Lubugu helped bring the project to success and was made Yelu and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 後率偏師，為西南邊大詳穩，從伐党項有功。

translations.literal: Later he led a detached column, served as grand commander of the southwestern frontier, and had merit in campaigns against the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded a detached force as grand commander of the southwestern frontier and distinguished himself in campaigns against the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 會河東節度使石敬瑭為其主所討，遣人求援，魯不古導送於朝，如其請。

translations.literal: When Hedong military commissioner Shi Jingtang was attacked by his sovereign and sent men to beg aid, Lubugu guided the envoys to court and granted the request as asked.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong commissioner Shi Jingtang was attacked by his lord and sent envoys seeking help, Lubugu conducted them to court and the throne granted what they asked.

sentences.zh: 帝親率師往援，魯不古從擊唐將張敬達於太原北，敗之。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally led troops to the rescue; Lubugu followed in striking Tang general Zhang Jingda north of Taiyuan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the army in person to relieve him; Lubugu joined the attack on Tang general Zhang Jingda north of Taiyuan and routed him.

sentences.zh: 會同初，從討党項，俘獲最諸將，師還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he followed in campaigning against the Tangut; his captives were the most among the generals, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong he campaigned against the Tangut and took more captives than any other commander before the army returned.

sentences.zh: 天祿中，拜於越。

translations.literal: During Tianlu he was appointed Yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianlu period he received the title Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 六年，為北院大王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became Great King of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was made Great King of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 終年五十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽，本姓劉，恒山人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou, originally surnamed Liu, was a man of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, whose original surname was Liu, came from Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 父邟，令蓚。

translations.literal: His father Kuang was magistrate of Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuang had been magistrate of Shuo.

sentences.zh: 梁開平初，滄州節度使劉守文陷蓚，其稗將趙德鈞獲延壽，養以為子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang Kaiping, Cangzhou military commissioner Liu Shouwen took Shuo; his lieutenant Zhao Dejun captured Yanshou and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang's Kaiping era, when Cangzhou commissioner Liu Shouwen seized Shuo, his officer Zhao Dejun captured Yanshou and adopted him.

sentences.zh: 少美容貌，好書史。

translations.literal: In youth he had a handsome countenance and loved books and history.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was handsome and devoted to books and history.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗先以女妻之，及即位，封其女為興平公主，拜延壽駙馬都尉、樞密使。

translations.literal: Tang Mingzong had first given him a daughter in marriage; when he took the throne he enfeoffed the daughter as Princess of Xingping and appointed Yanshou imperial son-in-law and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong of Tang had first married him to a daughter; on his accession he enfeoffed her as Princess of Xingping and made Yanshou imperial son-in-law and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明宗子從榮恃權跋扈，內外莫不震懾，延壽求補外避之，出為宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Mingzong's son Congrong relied on power and was overbearing; within and without none failed to tremble before him; Yanshou sought an outside posting to avoid him and went out as military commissioner of Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong's son Congrong swaggered with unchecked power, and everyone at court and beyond feared him; Yanshou asked for an outside appointment to escape him and was sent out as commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，加魯國公，復為樞密使，鎮許州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made Duke of Lu and again commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, garrisoning Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he was ennobled Duke of Lu, restored as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and stationed at Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭發兵太原，唐遣張敬達往討。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang raised troops at Taiyuan; Tang sent Zhang Jingda to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang rebelled from Taiyuan, Tang dispatched Zhang Jingda against him.

sentences.zh: 會敬達敗保晉安寨，延壽與德鈞往救，聞晉安已破，走團柏峪。

translations.literal: When Jingda was defeated and held Jin'an Stockade, Yanshou and Dejun went to the rescue; hearing Jin'an had fallen, they fled to Tuanbai Valley.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingda was beaten back to Jin'an Stockade, Yanshou and Dejun marched to relieve him; learning that Jin'an had fallen, they retreated to Tuanbai Valley.

sentences.zh: 太宗追及，延壽與其父俱降。

translations.literal: Taizong overtook them; Yanshou and his father both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong caught up with them, and Yanshou surrendered together with his father.

sentences.zh: 明年，德鈞卒，以延壽為幽州節度使，封燕王。

translations.literal: The next year Dejun died; Yanshou was made military commissioner of You Prefecture and enfeoffed Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after Dejun's death, Yanshou was appointed military commissioner of You Prefecture and enfeoffed Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 及改幽州為南京，遷留守，總山南事。

translations.literal: When You Prefecture was renamed the Southern Capital, he was transferred to garrison commander and given overall charge of affairs south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When You was redesignated the Southern Capital, he became its garrison commander with overall authority south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 天顯末，以延壽妻在晉，詔取之以歸。

translations.literal: Late in Tianxian, because Yanshou's wife was in Jin, an edict ordered her brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Tianxian, since Yanshou's wife remained in Jin, the court ordered her fetched home.

sentences.zh: 自是益自激昂圖報。

translations.literal: From this he grew all the more ardent in plotting repayment.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he burned all the hotter to repay the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 會同初，帝幸其第，加政事令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong the Emperor visited his residence and added the title Director of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong the Emperor visited his mansion and made him Director of Affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，晉人背盟，帝親征，延壽為先鋒，下貝州，授魏、博等州節度使，封魏王。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year the Jin people broke the alliance; the Emperor campaigned in person; Yanshou was vanguard, took Bei Prefecture, and was made military commissioner of Wei, Bo, and other prefectures and enfeoffed Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year six, when Jin broke the treaty, the Emperor marched in person with Yanshou as vanguard; he took Bei Prefecture and was made commissioner of Wei, Bo, and neighboring prefectures and enfeoffed Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 敗晉軍於南樂，獲其將賽項羽。

translations.literal: He defeated Jin troops at Nanle and captured their general Sai Xiangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Jin forces at Nanle and took their general Sai Xiangyu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 軍元城，晉將李守貞、高行周率兵來逆，破之。

translations.literal: The army was at Yuan Prefecture; Jin generals Li Shouzhen and Gao Xingzhou led troops to oppose and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuan Prefecture, Jin generals Li Shouzhen and Gao Xingzhou came out to meet him and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 至頓丘，會大霖雨，帝欲班師，延壽諫曰：「晉軍屯河濱，不敢出戰，若徑入澶州，奪其橋，則晉不足平。

translations.literal: Reaching Dunqiu, there came great continuous rain; the Emperor wished to withdraw the army; Yanshou remonstrated, saying: "Jin troops are encamped on the riverbank and dare not come out to fight; if we go straight into Cang Prefecture and seize their bridge, Jin will not be hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: At Dunqiu a torrential rain fell and the Emperor wanted to turn back; Yanshou urged, "The Jin army is camped along the river and will not come out; if we march straight on Cang Prefecture and seize their bridge, Jin will not be difficult to subdue.

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 適晉軍先歸澶州，高行周至析城，延壽將輕兵逆戰；

translations.literal: Just then Jin troops had already withdrawn to Cang Prefecture; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng; Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;
translations.idiomatic: By then the Jin army had already pulled back to Cang Prefecture and Gao Xingzhou had reached Xicheng; Yanshou led light troops to meet them;

sentences.zh: 上親督騎士突其陣，敵遂潰。

translations.literal: the Emperor personally directed the horsemen in charging their formation, and the enemy thereupon broke.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor personally drove the cavalry into their line and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 師還，留延壽徇貝、冀、深三州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Yanshou was left to pacify Bei, Ji, and Shen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, Yanshou was left to secure Bei, Ji, and Shen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 八年，再伐晉，晉主遣延壽族人趙行實以書來招。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again campaigned against Jin; the Jin ruler sent Yanshou's clansman Zhao Xingshi with a letter to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, on a second campaign against Jin, the Jin ruler sent Yanshou's kinsman Zhao Xingshi with a letter to win him over.

sentences.zh: 時晉人堅壁不出，延壽紿曰：「我陷虜久，寧忘父母之邦？

translations.literal: At the time the Jin people held their walls and would not come out; Yanshou deceived them, saying: "I have long been trapped among the barbarians — would I forget the land of my parents?
translations.idiomatic: While the Jin forces stayed behind their walls, Yanshou lied to them: "I have been captive among foreigners so long — would I forget my native land?

sentences.zh: 若以軍逆，我即歸。

translations.literal: If you send an army to meet me, I will at once return.
translations.idiomatic: Send an army to receive me and I will come back at once.

sentences.zh: 」晉人以為然，遣杜重威率兵迎之。

translations.literal: " The Jin people believed it and sent Du Chongwei with troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jin believed him and dispatched Du Chongwei with an army to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 延壽至滹沱河，據中渡橋，與晉軍力戰，手殺其將王清，兩軍相拒。

translations.literal: Yanshou reached the Hutuo River, held Zhongdu Bridge, and fought Jin troops hand to hand; he personally killed their general Wang Qing; the two armies faced each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou came to the Hutuo River, seized Zhongdu Bridge, and fought the Jin at close quarters, personally killing their general Wang Qing while the two armies locked in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 太宗潛由他渡濟，留延壽與耶律朔古據橋，敵不能奪，屢敗之，杜重威掃厥眾降。

translations.literal: Taizong secretly crossed by another ford; he left Yanshou and Yelu Shuogu to hold the bridge; the enemy could not take it; he repeatedly defeated them, and Du Chongwei swept his whole host into surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong crossed by a hidden ford, leaving Yanshou and Yelu Shuogu to defend the bridge; the enemy could not wrest it away, suffered repeated defeats, and Du Chongwei surrendered his entire force.

sentences.zh: 上喜，賜延壽龍鳳赭袍，且曰：「漢兵皆爾所有，爾宜親往撫慰。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased, bestowed on Yanshou a dragon-and-phoenix ochre robe, and said: "All the Han troops are now yours; you ought to go in person to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Emperor gave Yanshou a dragon-and-phoenix ochre robe and said, "All these Han soldiers are yours now; you should go yourself to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 」延壽至營，杜重威、李守貞迎謁馬首。

translations.literal: " Yanshou reached the camp; Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen came forward to greet him at his horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yanshou reached the camp, Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen came out to welcome him at his stirrup.

sentences.zh: 高模翰，一名松，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Mohan, also named Song, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mohan, also known as Song, was a Bohai native.

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善騎射，好談兵。

translations.literal: He had great physical strength, was skilled at mounted archery, and loved to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Powerfully built, expert in mounted archery, he delighted in talk of war.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖平渤海，模翰避地高麗，王妻以女。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Taizu pacified Bohai, Mohan took refuge in Koryo; the king gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first subdued Bohai, Mohan fled to Koryo, whose king married him to a princess.

sentences.zh: 因罪亡歸。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: After committing an offense he fled home again.

sentences.zh: 坐使酒殺人下獄，太祖知其才，貰之。

translations.literal: For making wine and killing a man he was imprisoned; Taizu knew his talent and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was jailed for drunkenness and manslaughter, but Taizu recognized his ability and let him go.

sentences.zh: 天顯十一年七月，唐遣張敬達、楊光遠帥師五十萬攻太原，勢銳甚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang sent Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan leading five hundred thousand troops to attack Taiyuan; their momentum was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianxian year eleven, Tang sent Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan with five hundred thousand men against Taiyuan in overwhelming force.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭遣人求救，太宗許之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang sent men to beg rescue; Taizong promised it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang sent envoys begging aid, and Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，征兵出雁門，模翰與敬達軍接戰，敗之，太原圍解。

translations.literal: In the ninth month troops were levied out through Yanmen; Mohan joined battle with Jingda's army and defeated it; the siege of Taiyuan was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army marched out through Yanmen Pass; Mohan met Jingda's force in battle, routed it, and lifted the siege of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭夜出謁帝，約為父子。

translations.literal: Jingtang came out by night to call on the Emperor and agreed to become father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang slipped out by night to see the Emperor and pledged himself as a son.

sentences.zh: 帝召模翰等賜以酒饌，親饗士卒，士氣益振。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Mohan and others, bestowed wine and food, and personally feasted the soldiers; morale grew still stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor called Mohan and the others, gave them food and wine, and feasted the troops in person, and their spirit rose higher still.

sentences.zh: 翌日，復戰，又敗之。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again and won another victory.

sentences.zh: 敬達鼠竄晉安寨，模翰獻俘於帝。

translations.literal: Jingda scurried like a rat into Jin'an Stockade; Mohan presented captives to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda scuttled into Jin'an Stockade like a cornered rat; Mohan presented prisoners to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 會敬瑭自立為晉帝，光遠斬敬達以降，諸州悉下。

translations.literal: When Jingtang declared himself Jin Emperor, Guangyuan beheaded Jingda to surrender; all prefectures submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingtang proclaimed himself Jin emperor, Guangyuan killed Jingda and surrendered, and the prefectures fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 上諭模翰曰：「朕自起兵，百餘戰，卿功第一，雖古名將無以加。

translations.literal: The Emperor addressed Mohan, saying: "From the time I first raised troops I have fought more than a hundred battles; your merit ranks first — even famous generals of old cannot surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Mohan, "Since I first took up arms I have fought more than a hundred battles, and your merit stands first — even the great commanders of antiquity cannot match it.

sentences.zh: 」乃授上將軍。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed him Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed him Grand General.

sentences.zh: 會同元年，冊禮告成，宴百官及諸國使於二儀殿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huitong, when the investiture rites were completed, he feasted the hundred officials and envoys of the various states in the Hall of the Two Principles.
translations.idiomatic: In Huitong year one, after the enthronement ceremonies, he banqueted officials and foreign envoys in the Hall of the Two Principles.

sentences.zh: 帝指模翰曰：「此國之勇將，朕統一天下，斯人之力也。

translations.literal: The Emperor pointed to Mohan and said: "This is the state's brave general; in my unifying the realm under Heaven, it is this man's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing at Mohan, the Emperor said, "Here is the empire's fiercest warrior; in bringing the realm under one rule, it is his strength that has done it.

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " The assembled ministers all shouted "Long live the Emperor!" ten thousand times.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole assembly shouted ten thousand blessings for long life.

sentences.zh: 及晉叛盟，出師南伐。

translations.literal: When Jin broke the alliance, troops marched south to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin broke the treaty, the army marched south.

sentences.zh: 模翰為統軍副使，與僧遏前驅，拔赤城，破德、貝諸寨。

translations.literal: Mohan was deputy commander-in-chief; with Senge he advanced as vanguard, took Chicheng, and stormed the stockades of De and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Mohan served as deputy commander-in-chief; with Senge in the van he seized Chicheng and stormed the camps at De and Bei.

sentences.zh: 是冬，兼總左右鐵鷂子軍，下關南城邑數十。

translations.literal: That winter he also commanded the left and right Iron Hawk armies and took several dozen walled places south of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he also took overall command of the left and right Iron Hawk armies and reduced dozens of walled towns south of the pass.

sentences.zh: 三月，敕虎官楊覃赴乾寧軍，為滄州節度使田武名所圍，模翰與趙延壽聚議往救。

translations.literal: In the third month the Tiger Office officer Yang Tan went to Qianning Army; he was besieged by Cangzhou military commissioner Tian Wuming; Mohan and Zhao Yanshou met in council to march to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, when Tiger Office officer Yang Tan was sent to Qianning Army and besieged by Cangzhou commissioner Tian Wuming, Mohan and Zhao Yanshou agreed to go to his relief.

sentences.zh: 俄有光自模翰目中出，縈繞旗矛，焰焰如流星久之。

translations.literal: Soon a light issued from Mohan's eye, coiling around flag and spear, blazing like a meteor for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a light shot from Mohan's eye and wound around his banner and spear, flaring like a meteor for some time.

sentences.zh: 模翰喜曰：「此天贊之祥！

translations.literal: Mohan rejoiced and said: "This is a heaven-sent auspice!
translations.idiomatic: Mohan exclaimed in joy, "This is Heaven's blessing on us!

sentences.zh: 」遂進兵，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: " He thereupon advanced; kills and captures were very many.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed the attack at once and the slaughter and captures were immense.

sentences.zh: 以功加侍中。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 略地鹽山，破饒安，晉人震怖，不敢接戰。

translations.literal: He overran the land of Yanshan, stormed Rao'an, and the Jin people were shaken with terror and dared not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: He overran Yanshan, took Rao'an, and the Jin were so terrified they would not stand and fight.

sentences.zh: 加太傅。

translations.literal: He was further made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 晉以魏府節度使杜重威領兵三十萬來拒，模翰謂左右曰：「軍法在正不在多。

translations.literal: Jin sent Wei Prefecture military commissioner Du Chongwei leading three hundred thousand troops to resist; Mohan said to those beside him: "Military law lies in rectitude, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Wei commissioner Du Chongwei with three hundred thousand men to oppose him; Mohan told his staff, "The art of war rests on discipline, not on numbers.

sentences.zh: 以多陵少，不義必敗。

translations.literal: To use the many to overwhelm the few is unrighteous and must fail.
translations.idiomatic: To crush the few with the many is unjust and bound to fail.

sentences.zh: 其晉之謂乎！

translations.literal: Is this not what Jin means?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not exactly Jin's mistake?

sentences.zh: 」詰旦，以麾下三百人逆戰，殺其先鋒梁漢璋，餘兵敗走。

translations.literal: " At dawn the next day he met the enemy with three hundred men under his command, killed their vanguard Liang Hanzhang, and the rest of the troops fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn he led three hundred of his own men into the fight, killed their vanguard Liang Hanzhang, and the rest broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 手詔褒美，比漢之李陵。

translations.literal: An imperial letter in the Emperor's own hand praised him, comparing him to Han's Li Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote him a personal commendation, likening him to Li Ling of Han.

sentences.zh: 頃之，杜重威等復至滹沱河，帝召模翰問計。

translations.literal: Before long Du Chongwei and the others again came to the Hutuo River; the Emperor summoned Mohan to ask his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Du Chongwei and his colleagues returned to the Hutuo River, and the Emperor called Mohan in for counsel.

sentences.zh: 上善其言曰：「諸將莫及此。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words, saying: "Among the generals none can match this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved, saying, "None of the other commanders can equal this.

sentences.zh: 」乃令模翰守中渡橋。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Mohan to hold Zhongdu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Mohan to defend Zhongdu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 及戰，復敗之，上曰：「朕憑高觀兩軍之勢，顧卿英銳無敵，如鷹逐雉兔。

translations.literal: When battle was joined he again defeated them; the Emperor said: "I watched from a height the momentum of the two armies; seeing you fierce and unmatched, like an eagle pursuing pheasant and hare.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting he routed them again; the Emperor said, "From the height I watched both armies; you were fierce beyond compare, like an eagle stooping on pheasant and hare.

sentences.zh: 當圖形麟閣，爵貤後裔。

translations.literal: Your likeness should be painted in the Qilin Pavilion, and noble rank passed down to your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Your portrait belongs in the Qilin Pavilion, and noble rank should descend to your heirs.

sentences.zh: 」已而杜重威等降。

translations.literal: " Before long Du Chongwei and the others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Du Chongwei and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 車駕入汴，加特進檢校太師，封悊郡開國公，賜璽書、劍器。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Bian, Mohan was made special emissary and acting Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed Duke of Yi Commandery with state-founding rank, and bestowed imperial writ and sword regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When the court entered Bian, Mohan was promoted to special emissary and acting Grand Preceptor, created Duke of Yi Commandery with state-founding rank, and given imperial writ and ceremonial sword.

sentences.zh: 為汴州巡檢使，平汜水諸山土賊，遷鎮中京。

translations.literal: He was made inspector of Bian Prefecture, pacified the mountain bandits of the Si River region, and was transferred to garrison the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of Bian Prefecture he subdued the mountain bandits along the Si River, then was transferred to garrison the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 天祿二年，加開府儀同三司，賜對衣、鞍勒、名馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianlu he was made Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an open office equal to the Three Excellencies and was given matching robes, saddle and bridle, and a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianlu year two he received the rank of Grand Master of the Palace with open-office privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, together with court robes, saddle gear, and a celebrated horse.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，召為中臺省右相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he was summoned as Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingli he was recalled to serve as Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至東京，父老歡迎曰：「公起戎行，致身富貴，為鄉里榮，相如、買臣輩不足過也。

translations.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital, the elders welcomed him, saying: "You rose from the army to wealth and honor and brought glory to your home district — men like Xiangru and Maichén cannot surpass you.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the Eastern Capital, the local elders hailed him: "You rose from the ranks to wealth and honor and made your district proud — not even Xiangru or Maichén could outdo you.

sentences.zh: 」九年正月，遷左相，卒。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the ninth year he was transferred to Left Chancellor and died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of year nine he was made Left Chancellor, and soon after died.

sentences.zh: 趙思溫，字文美，盧龍人。

translations.literal: Zhao Siwen, style name Wenmei, was a man of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Siwen, whose style name was Wenmei, came from Lulong.

sentences.zh: 少果銳，膂力兼人，隸燕帥劉仁恭幕。

translations.literal: In youth he was resolute and sharp; his strength matched several men; he served on the staff of Yan commander Liu Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and keen, possessed the strength of several men, and entered the staff of Yan commander Liu Rengong.

sentences.zh: 李存勖問罪於燕，思溫統偏師拒之。

translations.literal: When Li Cunxu brought charges against Yan, Siwen commanded a detached force to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cunxu marched against Yan, Siwen led a detached column to hold him off.

sentences.zh: 流矢中目，裂裳漬血，戰猶不已。

translations.literal: A stray arrow struck his eye; he tore his robe to soak the blood and still would not cease fighting.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck his eye; he ripped his robe to staunch the blood and kept fighting without pause.

sentences.zh: 為存勖將周德威所擒，存勖壯而釋其縛。

translations.literal: He was captured by Cunxu's general Zhou Dewei; Cunxu admired him and released his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei, Cunxu's general, took him prisoner; Cunxu was impressed and had his bonds cut.

sentences.zh: 久之，日見信用。

translations.literal: After a long while he came to be trusted day by day.
translations.idiomatic: In time he won the ruler's trust day by day.

sentences.zh: 與梁戰於莘縣，以驍勇聞，授平州刺史，兼平、營、薊三州都指揮使。

translations.literal: In battle with Liang at Shen County he became known for fierce courage and was made prefect of Ping, concurrently commander-in-chief of Ping, Ying, and Ji prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting Liang at Shen County, he won fame for reckless bravery and was appointed prefect of Ping and overall commander of Ping, Ying, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 神冊二年，太祖遣大將經略燕地，思溫來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shence, Taizu sent a great general to campaign in the Yan region; Siwen came over and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In Shence year two, when Taizu sent a great general to operate in Yan territory, Siwen defected to him.

sentences.zh: 及伐渤海，以思溫為漢軍都團練使，力戰，拔扶餘城。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Bohai, Siwen was made regimental commander of the Han army; he fought fiercely and stormed Fuyu city.
translations.idiomatic: On the Bohai campaign he was made regimental commander of the Han forces, fought hard, and took Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 身被數創，太祖親為調藥。

translations.literal: His body bore many wounds; Taizu personally prepared medicine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded many times over, he was tended with medicine mixed by Taizu himself.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以功擢檢校太保、保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, for his merit he was promoted acting Grand Guardian and military commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession he was raised to acting Grand Guardian and commissioner of the Baojing Army for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 天顯十一年，唐兵攻太原，石敬瑭遣使求救，上命思溫自嵐、憲間出兵援之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang troops attacked Taiyuan; Shi Jingtang sent envoys to beg rescue; the Emperor ordered Siwen to march out between Lan and Xian to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year eleven, when Tang besieged Taiyuan and Shi Jingtang begged aid, the Emperor ordered Siwen to advance through the Lan and Xian corridor to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 既罷兵，改南京留守、盧龍軍節度使、管內觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司，兼侍中，賜協謀靜亂翊聖功臣，尋改臨海軍節度使。

translations.literal: After the fighting ceased he was made garrison commander of the Southern Capital, military commissioner of Lulong Army, commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit, Grand Master of the Palace with open-office privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and concurrently Palace Attendant; he was granted the title of merit-bearing Worthy Who Assists in Planning and Pacifying Disorder; soon after he was transferred to military commissioner of Linhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: When hostilities ended he became garrison commander of the Southern Capital, Lulong commissioner, circuit observer and disposer, Grand Master of the Palace with Three-Excellency privileges, and Palace Attendant, with the merit title Worthy Who Assists in Planning and Pacifying Disorder; he was soon transferred to commissioner of the Linhai Army.

sentences.zh: 會同初，從耶律牒摐使晉行冊禮，還，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he followed Yelu Diezeng on an embassy to Jin to perform the investiture rites; on his return he was made acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong he accompanied Yelu Diezeng to Jin for the enthronement mission and, on returning, was made acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 二年，有星隕於庭，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year a star fell in his courtyard; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year two a meteor fell in his courtyard, and he died.

sentences.zh: 上遣使賻祭，贈太師、魏國公。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys with funeral gifts and sacrifices and posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys with funeral gifts and posthumously created him Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子延照、延靖，官至使相。

translations.literal: His sons Yanzhao and Yanjing rose to the rank of commissioner-envoy.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yanzhao and Yanjing both rose to commissioner-envoy rank.

sentences.zh: 耶律漚裏思，六院夷離堇蒲古只之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Oulisi was a descendant of Pugu Zhi, Yelu of the Six Courts.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Oulisi descended from Pugu Zhi, who had been Yelu of the Six Courts.

sentences.zh: 負勇略，每戰被重鎧，揮鐵槊，所向披靡。

translations.literal: He possessed courage and stratagem; in every battle he wore heavy armor and wielded an iron spear; wherever he went none could withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resourceful in war, he always fought in heavy armor with an iron spear and swept aside all who faced him.

sentences.zh: 會同間，伐晉，上至河而獵，適海東青鶻搏雉，晉人隔水以鴿引去。

translations.literal: During Huitong, campaigning against Jin, the Emperor went to the river to hunt; just then an eastern-sea goshawk struck a pheasant, and Jin men across the water lured it away with a pigeon.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huitong campaign against Jin, while the Emperor hunted by the river, an eastern-sea goshawk stooped on a pheasant and Jin men across the water lured the bird off with a pigeon.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「誰為我得此人？

translations.literal: The Emperor looked to those beside him and said: "Who will get this man for me?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor turned to his attendants and asked, "Who will fetch that man for me?

sentences.zh: 」漚裏思請內廄馬，濟河擒之，並殺救者數人還。

translations.literal: " Oulisi asked for a horse from the inner stables, crossed the river, seized him, and also killed several of the rescuers before returning.
translations.idiomatic: " Oulisi took a horse from the imperial stables, crossed the river, captured the falconer, killed several of his rescuers, and came back.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，優加賞賚。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with special generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 既而晉將杜重威逆於望都，據水勒戰。

translations.literal: Before long Jin general Du Chongwei opposed him at Wangdu and held the water line to force battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin general Du Chongwei met him at Wangdu, holding the river line to compel a fight.

sentences.zh: 漚裏思介馬突陣，余軍繼之。

translations.literal: Oulisi spurred his horse and charged the formation; the rest of the army followed.
translations.idiomatic: Oulisi spurred forward alone into the enemy line, and the main body followed.

sentences.zh: 被圍，眾言陣薄處可出，漚裏思曰：「恐彼有他備。

translations.literal: When surrounded, the masses said a thin place in the formation could be used to break out; Oulisi said: "I fear they have other preparations there.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded, his men pointed to a thin spot in the line as an escape; Oulisi said, "They may have laid another trap there.

sentences.zh: 」竟引兵沖堅而出；

translations.literal: " In the end he led troops in a charge through the solid center and broke out;
translations.idiomatic: " He drove instead through the thick of the enemy and broke free;

sentences.zh: 回視眾所指，皆大塹也。

translations.literal: looking back where the crowd had pointed, all were great trenches.
translations.idiomatic: and when he looked back at the gap his men had urged, it was all deep trenches.

sentences.zh: 其料敵多此類。

translations.literal: His reading of the enemy was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment of the enemy was often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 是年，總領敵烈皮室軍，坐私免部曲，奪官，卒。

translations.literal: That year he took overall command of the Dilie Pishi army; for privately releasing troops from his command he was stripped of office and died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, while commanding the Dilie Pishi army, he was dismissed for privately releasing men from his unit and soon died.

sentences.zh: 張礪，磁州人，初仕唐為掌書記，遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: Zhang Li, a man of Cizhou, at first served Tang as secretarial aide and was promoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li of Cizhou first served Tang as a secretarial aide and rose to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 會石敬瑭起兵，唐主以礪為招討判官，從趙德鈞援張敬達於河東。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang raised troops, the Tang ruler made Li staff judge of the pacification campaign and sent him with Zhao Dejun to relieve Zhang Jingda in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the Tang emperor made Li a staff judge on the punitive campaign and sent him with Zhao Dejun to relieve Zhang Jingda in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 及敬達敗，礪入契丹。

translations.literal: When Jingda was defeated, Li entered Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingda's defeat, Li passed into Khitan service.

sentences.zh: 後太宗見礪剛直有文彩，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: Later Taizong saw that Li was upright and possessed literary talent and promoted him Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizong, seeing Li's integrity and literary gifts, made him Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 礪臨事必盡言，無所避，上益重之。

translations.literal: In handling affairs Li always spoke his full mind without avoidance, and the Emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Li spoke his mind fully on every matter without flinching, and the Emperor prized him all the more.

sentences.zh: 未幾，謀亡歸，為追騎所獲。

translations.literal: Before long he plotted to flee home and was seized by pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he plotted escape to his homeland and was caught by pursuit riders.

sentences.zh: 上責曰：「汝何故亡？

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him, saying: "Why did you flee?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him: "Why did you run away?

sentences.zh: 」礪對曰：「臣不習北方土俗，飲食居處，意常郁郁，以是亡耳。

translations.literal: " Li replied: "Your servant is not accustomed to northern customs in food and dwelling; my mind was always depressed, and for that reason I fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Li answered, "I never grew used to northern food and ways of living; I was always miserable, and that is why I fled.

sentences.zh: 」上顧通事高彥英曰：「朕嘗戒汝善遇此人，何乃使失所而亡？

translations.literal: " The Emperor turned to the interpreter Gao Yanying and said: "I once warned you to treat this man well — how could you let him lose his footing and flee?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor turned to interpreter Gao Yanying: "I told you to treat this man well — how did you let him grow so wretched that he fled?

sentences.zh: 礪去，可再得耶？

translations.literal: If Li is gone, can he be gotten again?
translations.idiomatic: If Li is lost, can we get him back?

sentences.zh: 」遂杖彥英而謝礪。

translations.literal: " He thereupon had Yanying beaten and apologized to Li.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Yanying beaten on the spot and apologized to Li.

sentences.zh: 會同初，升翰林承旨，兼吏部尚書，從太宗伐晉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he was promoted Hanlin commissioner and concurrently Minister of Personnel, and followed Taizong in campaigning against Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong he was made Hanlin commissioner and Minister of Personnel and followed Taizong on the Jin campaign.

sentences.zh: 入汴，諸將蕭翰、耶律郎五、麻答輩肆殺掠，礪奏曰：「今大遼始得中國，宜以中國人治之，不可專用國人及左右近習。

translations.literal: After entering Bian, the generals Xiao Han, Yelu Langwu, Mada, and their like wantonly killed and plundered; Li memorialized, saying: "Now that Great Liao has just obtained China, China ought to be governed by Chinese; one cannot rely solely on countrymen and close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: After Bian fell, generals such as Xiao Han, Yelu Langwu, and Mada looted at will; Li memorialized: "Great Liao has only just taken China — China should be ruled by Chinese; you cannot govern it solely through Khitan and personal favorites.

sentences.zh: 茍政令乖失，則人心不服，雖得之亦將失之。

translations.literal: If government orders go astray, hearts will not submit; though you have gained it, you will yet lose it.
translations.idiomatic: If policy goes wrong, the people will not obey; even having won the realm, you will lose it again.

sentences.zh: 」上不聽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 改右僕射，兼門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: He was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Vice Minister of the Gate and Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Minister of the Gate, and Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，車駕北還，至欒城崩。

translations.literal: Before long the imperial carriage returned north; at Luancheng the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court turned north; at Luancheng the Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 時礪在恒州，蕭翰與麻答以兵圍其第。

translations.literal: At the time Li was at Heng Prefecture; Xiao Han and Mada surrounded his residence with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li was then at Heng Prefecture when Xiao Han and Mada surrounded his mansion with soldiers.

sentences.zh: 礪方臥病，出見之。

translations.literal: Li was then ill in bed but came out to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Though bedridden, he came out to face them.

sentences.zh: 翰數之曰：「汝何故於先帝言國人不可為節度使？

translations.literal: Han enumerated his offenses, saying: "Why did you tell the late Emperor that countrymen must not be made military commissioners?
translations.idiomatic: Han accused him: "Why did you tell the late Emperor that Khitan should not be made military commissioners?

sentences.zh: 我以國舅之親，有征伐功，先帝留我守汴，以為宣武軍節度使，汝獨以為不可。

translations.literal: I, by the closeness of an imperial brother-in-law and with merit in campaigns, was left by the late Emperor to guard Bian and made military commissioner of Xuanwu Army — you alone said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: I am the Emperor's brother-in-law and earned merit in war; the late Emperor left me to hold Bian as Xuanwu commissioner — you alone said I must not.

sentences.zh: 又譖我與解裏好掠人財物子女。

translations.literal: You also slandered me and Jieli for loving to plunder people's goods and women.
translations.idiomatic: You also slandered me and Jieli as men who loved to seize people's goods and daughters.

sentences.zh: 今必殺汝！

translations.literal: Today I shall certainly kill you!
translations.idiomatic: Today I will kill you!

sentences.zh: 」趣令鎖之。

translations.literal: " He hurriedly ordered him bound.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him bound at once.

sentences.zh: 礪抗聲曰：「此國家大體，安危所系，吾實言之。

translations.literal: Li answered in a ringing voice: "This is the great principle of the state, on which safety and peril depend — I spoke the truth of it.
translations.idiomatic: Li answered boldly: "This touches the state's fundamental interest and its safety — I spoke the truth.

sentences.zh: 欲殺即殺，奚以鎖為？

translations.literal: If you wish to kill, then kill — why bind me?
translations.idiomatic: Kill me if you will — why put me in chains?

sentences.zh: 」麻答以礪大臣，不可專殺，乃救止之。

translations.literal: " Mada said that as a great minister Li could not be killed on one's private authority, and so restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: " Mada said a great minister could not be murdered on private authority and stopped the killing.

sentences.zh: 是夕，礪恚憤卒。

translations.literal: That night Li died of indignant rage.
translations.idiomatic: That night Li died of outrage and grief.

sentences.zh: 論曰：初，晉因遼之兵而得天下，故兼臣禮而父事之，割地以為壽，輸帛以為貢。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the beginning Jin obtained the realm through Liao's troops, and therefore observed both minister and son rites in serving it as a father, ceding territory for longevity and sending silk as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: At first Jin won the realm with Liao's armies, and therefore treated Liao as both lord and father, ceding land for its favor and sending silk as tribute.

sentences.zh: 未久也，而會同之師次滹沱矣。

translations.literal: Not long after, the army of Huitong halted at the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Huitong armies were camped on the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 豈群帥貪功黷武而致然歟？

translations.literal: Was it that the host of commanders, greedy for merit, abused arms and brought this about?
translations.idiomatic: Was it because commanders greedy for glory abused their arms?

sentences.zh: 抑所謂信不由衷也哉？

translations.literal: Or was it what is called faith not proceeding from the heart?
translations.idiomatic: Or was it simply that their pledge was never sincere?

sentences.zh: 模翰以功名自終，可謂良將。

translations.literal: Mohan ended his life with fame and achievement intact — he may be called a good general.
translations.idiomatic: Mohan died with his fame intact — a true general.

sentences.zh: 若延壽之勛雖著，至於覬覦儲位，謬矣，利令智昏，固無足議。

translations.literal: As for Yanshou, though his merit was conspicuous, in coveting the heir's position he erred; profit makes wisdom dim — he is truly not worth discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou's achievements were great, but his eyeing of the succession was folly; gain blinded his judgment, and he scarcely merits debate.

sentences.zh: 若乃成末釁以虧俊功，如解裏者，何譏焉！

translations.literal: But to complete a late misstep and thereby mar splendid achievement — as with Jieli, what is there to reproach?
translations.idiomatic: Yet to let a late misstep tarnish an otherwise splendid record, as with Jieli — what fault is there to find?
